query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying an electrospark deposition surface treatment to form a protective, oxide-scale coating on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will significantly improve its oxygen resistance at high temperature without degrading its established mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibiting 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and yield strengths of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1.
generation.intervention: Use electrospark deposition to apply a thin, adherent protective coating (derived from a high-entropy alloy formulation similar to the base alloy or an oxidation-resistant variant) onto the alloy surface.
generation.conditions: Exposure at 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere (e.g., air) for an extended period (e.g., 100 hours) and under mechanical loading at strain rates between 10^−4 and 10^−2 s^−1.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a dense and adherent oxide scale acting as a diffusion barrier at the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: The electrospark-deposited coating rapidly forms or facilitates the formation of a stable, refractory oxide layer that retards oxygen diffusion into the alloy. This barrier minimizes further oxidation during high-temperature service, while preserving the underlying alloy’s mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coated specimens will display markedly reduced oxygen uptake and surface oxidation compared to uncoated samples, with retention of the original tensile ductility at room temperature and yield strength at 1000 °C.
generation.baseline: Untreated (cast) HfNbTaTiZr exhibits poor oxygen resistance under the same high-temperature conditions, leading to detrimental oxidation.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective under high-temperature (around 1000 °C) conditions in air with specified mechanical strain rates; its efficacy under thermal cycling or significantly different atmospheres remains to be validated.
generation.uncertainty: Long-term coating stability and its performance during repeated thermal cycling or under varying oxygen partial pressures are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of cast HfNbTaTiZr samples. Apply the electrospark deposition coating to one set (intervention group) while leaving the other set uncoated (control group). Subject both groups to 1000 °C in ambient air for 100 hours while maintaining strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1 during mechanical loading.
measurements: Quantify the degree of oxidation using weight-gain measurements, XPS analysis, and SEM/EDS surface characterizations.
Evaluate mechanical performance by measuring room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength post-exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the electrospark-deposited coated samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in oxidation or if their mechanical properties (ductility and yield strength) decline significantly compared to the control samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe aim of the present paper is to investigate an innovative high corrosion resistance coating realized by electrospark deposition. The coating material was fabricated from HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy. HEA was produced by the mechanical alloying of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr high-purity powders in a planetary ball mill, achieving a good homogenization and a high alloying degree, followed by spark plasma sintering consolidation. The electrodes for electrospark deposition were cut and machined from the bulk material. Stainless steel specimens were coated and electrochemically tested for corrosion resistance in a 3.5% NaCl saline solution.Keywords: high-entropy alloy, mechanical alloying, corrosion resistance
## 1. Introduction
HEAs are systems of alloys consisting of at least five elements in equal or almost equal atomic proportions. The large number of alloying elements leads to the formation of disordered solid solutions that maximize the configurational entropy.
